clue.text: Retiring to devour a collection of books in shed

indicators.note: something devoured is taken inside, so the first piece swallows the others

parts.note: a retiring person is shy
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone bashfully wolfs down a set of books while hiding in the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude hut, the same kind of rough outbuilding as a shed.

clue.text: Flourished as rock musician finally

parts.note: to rock something is to shake it

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of musician

explanation.surface: A guitarist's showy gesture is compared to that of a rock star.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a stick or sword is to wave or brandish it, so a weapon flourished has been shaken.

clue.text: Stone mark on plate within a grand portal

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a portal is a gate or doorway
REG is a car's registration mark, shown on its number plate

explanation.surface: A stonemason carves a mark on a slab set into an imposing gateway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' looks like a material for the portal itself, but it is the definition; 'plate' means a car's number plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregate is the builder's term for crushed stone or gravel mixed into concrete.

clue.text: Confuse after final conversion to British pound

indicators.note: the last letter of the first word is converted into another letter

parts.note: to throw someone is to confuse or disconcert them

explanation.surface: Someone is bewildered by a currency change-over to sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: THROW has its final W converted to B.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound is to beat rhythmically, as a heart or headache does, which is what a throb is.

clue.text: Toughest weight: that is, for boxing?

indicators.note: boxing means putting into a box, so the small pieces are packed inside the container

parts.note: a chest is a box for keeping things in
IE (id est) is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A question about which weight class suits a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a boxing weight division; here 'boxing?' signals packing into a box, and 'for' stands for the container, a box for storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat or toffee that is toughest needs the most chewing, so it is the chewiest.

clue.text: Bad mood champion, before game, means to get over

parts.note: to have the hump is British slang for being in a sulk
to champion a cause is to back it
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A sulky title-holder before a match explains how to get past it.
explanation.walkthrough: A humpback bridge is a steeply arched road bridge, common on British country lanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Any bridge is a way of crossing a river or road, a means of getting over it.

clue.text: We aligned with movement taking broader views

indicators.note: movement says the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: We lined up and moved, seeing the bigger picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-angle lens is one that captures a broader field of view than a normal lens.

clue.text: Large article from Bild perhaps covers Scottish town

indicators.note: covers means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Bild is a German newspaper, and ein is a German indefinite article
LG is a common abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A big feature in the German tabloid Bild reports on a town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a town in Moray, in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Ambiguous when speaking, moreover, and gently moved

indicators.note: when speaking says the word is heard as spoken, not as written

parts.note: too means moreover or also
to edge is to move slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: A speaker is vague, and also shuffles about cautiously.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-edged remark cuts both ways, having a double meaning.

clue.text: Yet probably not allowing grannies to keep up?

definitions.text: Yet probably not allowing grannies to keep up?

parts.words: Yet probably not allowing grannies to keep up?
parts.note: grannies are elderly people who walk slowly, and also granny knots; a ship's speed is measured in knots

explanation.surface: Going so fast that the elderly cannot keep pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means very quickly, but the clue jokes that granny knots, being knots, might keep up after all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly, from a ship's speed measured in nautical miles per hour.

clue.text: Loath to get involved with grim process

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to take part in a grim procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.

clue.text: Leave after trouble, so as not to be seen

definitions.text: so as not to be seen

indicators.note: after places the word for leave second, behind the word for trouble

parts.note: to dog is to trouble or plague persistently
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone departs after a spot of bother to keep out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is old slang for keeping still and hidden, out of sight.

clue.text: Girl's uniform just too short

indicators.note: something just too short falls a little short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: even means uniform or level

explanation.surface: A girl's school uniform is a touch too short for her.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is a girl's name, that of the first woman in Genesis.

clue.text: Foolish girl showered with bachelor

parts.note: bird is British slang for a girl
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
rained means showered down

explanation.surface: A daft young woman got a soaking along with an unmarried man.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird-brained means having a brain like a bird's, so silly or scatterbrained.

clue.text: Big cheese intact after rolling around bags

indicators.note: rolling around says the selected letters are turned to read backwards
bags means holds inside, so the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A large cheese survives unharmed after being bowled about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' picks TACTAF out of 'intact after', and 'rolling around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is slang for an important person, and so is a fat cat, a wealthy bigwig.

clue.text: Kindly guy, possibly, I partner

parts.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent, an example of a cord
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A kindly man, perhaps, and I team up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordially means warmly and in a friendly way, as kindly does.

clue.text: Cold, looking back periodically, jealous of glam coat

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: looking back says the chosen letters are read in reverse order
periodically picks letters at regular intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: A frosty, envious glance backwards at someone's glamorous coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' picks ELUOGA from 'jealous of glam'; 'looking back' turns it into AGOULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoule is a lightweight hooded waterproof jacket.

clue.text: Veal ruins fancy blanket

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A fancy dish of veal ruins the bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket rule applies to every case, just as a universal one does.

clue.text: Seconds prepared with spices went fast!

parts.note: curried food is cooked with curry spices

explanation.surface: Second helpings of a spicy dish disappeared quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to hurry along with short quick steps.

clue.text: Root for instance, often initially is so long

parts.note: to root for a team is to cheer it on

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about cheering on something that happens often.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is a British informal goodbye, just like so long.

clue.text: Failed spectacularly to find mushroom

definitions.meaning: to have blown it is to have ruined a chance
an edible mushroom with a lilac tinge

explanation.surface: A mushroom-hunter's foraging trip goes badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Blew it is a phrase for failing badly; the blewit is an edible fungus with a bluish stem.

clue.text: Rent our people picked up for house

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: rent means tore, as in rent asunder, and our people are us, giving tore us

explanation.surface: Tenants pay rent and look for a house to share.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology the zodiac is divided into twelve houses, and Taurus, the bull, is one sign.

clue.text: Amusing kid with second language, missing nothing

parts.note: to kid someone is to rib or tease them
a tick is a moment or second

indicators.note: missing says one piece is left out of another

parts.note: lingo is informal for a language
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A child comes to a second language class but leaves something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rib-tickling describes something funny enough to make one laugh heartily.

clue.text: Strength of one designed to lift opponents with hands

parts.note: a bra is a garment designed to lift and support
in bridge the players holding hands are North, South, East and West, and West and North are opponents

explanation.surface: A weightlifter built to raise rivals with bare hands shows great power.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn is physical muscle, a word for bodily strength.

clue.text: Work, then rest: take five?

parts.note: a machine that goes is working
a nap is a short rest

explanation.surface: A worker takes a coffee break between bouts of labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Take five looks like a five-minute break, but in the card game nap, going nap is bidding to take all five tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game nap, the top bid commits the player to winning all five tricks in a hand.

clue.text: Letter from abroad and when it might reach us?

definitions.meaning: the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
the abbreviation for estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: Wondering when a letter from overseas will arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is a Greek letter; the same letters are short for estimated time of arrival.

clue.text: Everything considered unhealthy not available for consumption

indicators.note: consumed means eaten, so the first piece takes the second inside

parts.note: ill means unhealthy

explanation.surface: All things weighed up, unwholesome food is off the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means taking everything into account, all told.

clue.text: Runner who's old unexpectedly regains lead in race

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly is out of order, so these letters are rearranged
lead in takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A veteran athlete surprisingly retakes the lead in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete, which the surface feeds, but here it means someone who runs things.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner of an event or business is the person who manages or arranges it.

clue.text: Ruin besetting chap always turned out well?

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to dish someone's hopes is to ruin them
Andy is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: Disaster surrounds a man who always dressed smartly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy takes great care over clothes, so dandyish means habitually smartly turned out.

clue.text: Missing software downloads briefly bearing fruit

parts.note: an app is a software application downloaded to a phone

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: less means without or missing, as a suffix

explanation.surface: Someone without their downloaded programs is still productive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing software downloads' gives APPLESS (without apps), and 'briefly' trims its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Apples are a common orchard fruit.
